slot.brief: Short 4-part sentence (P, Q, R, S) that must be rearranged into a grammatical whole; options give order combinations.

stem:
Arrange P, Q, R and S to complete the sentence meaningfully.

The curator displayed the painting

P. only after
Q. a laboratory test showed
R. that its pigment would not fade
S. when exposed to sunlight.

verdicts.working: P→Q→R→S gives: “The curator displayed the painting only after a laboratory test showed that its pigment would not fade when exposed to sunlight.”

working:
P begins the required “only after” clause; Q supplies its subject and verb; R is the test’s “that” clause; S completes “would not fade when exposed to sunlight.” Only PQRS preserves these grammatical links.

Independent check: P→Q→R→S gives: “The curator displayed the painting only after a laboratory test showed that its pigment would not fade when exposed to sunlight.”
solution: P begins the time clause, followed by Q’s subject and verb; R completes the test’s “that” clause, and S completes “would not fade.” The sequence is PQRS.
